questions.q: What is a real prerequisite step before running CREATE AVAILABILITY GROUP, per this lesson?
options: Installing SQL Server Reporting Services on every replica
Enabling the Always On Availability Groups feature on each instance via SQL Server Configuration Manager, which requires a service restart
Setting the database to SIMPLE recovery model
Disabling Windows Server Failover Clustering
questions.explain: Always On must be enabled per instance through Configuration Manager, which requires a SQL Server service restart, before any AG can be created.

questions.q: What infrastructure do AG replicas reuse for replica-to-replica communication, per this lesson?
options: The default SQL Server instance port only, with no separate endpoint
SQL Server Reporting Services web endpoints
Database mirroring endpoints, typically on TCP port 5022
SMTP mail endpoints
questions.explain: AGs reuse the database mirroring endpoint infrastructure, commonly configured on TCP port 5022, for communication between replicas.

questions.q: Why must the database be restored with the NORECOVERY option before joining it to an Availability Group?
options: NORECOVERY is not actually required; any restore option works
NORECOVERY is required only for FULL recovery model databases, unrelated to AGs
NORECOVERY permanently deletes the database's transaction log
NORECOVERY leaves the database in a restoring state so SQL Server can still apply incoming log records from the primary — a fully recovered database can't be joined
questions.explain: A database must remain in a restoring (non-recovered) state to accept the ongoing stream of log records from the primary; NORECOVERY achieves that, while a normal recovered restore does not.

questions.q: What does automatic seeding (SEEDING_MODE = AUTOMATIC) do, per this lesson?
options: It disables the need for a listener
It automatically creates the WSFC cluster
It automatically promotes a secondary to primary during failover
It has SQL Server stream the initial data to the secondary over the network, instead of requiring a manual backup and restore
questions.explain: Automatic seeding lets SQL Server transfer the initial database contents over the network directly, as an alternative to the manual backup/restore process — convenient for smaller databases.

questions.q: A DBA restores a database normally, bringing it fully online, then tries to join it to an AG. What needs to happen, per this lesson?
options: The database needs to be switched to SIMPLE recovery model first
Nothing — a fully recovered database can join an AG without any changes
The restore needs to be redone with the NORECOVERY option so the database is left in a restoring state that can accept log records from the primary
The AG itself needs to be dropped and recreated
questions.explain: Joining an AG requires the database to be in a restoring state (via NORECOVERY); a fully recovered, online database must be restored again with NORECOVERY before the join can succeed.
